hypotheses.paper: (i) open causally convex neighbourhood U_p carrying a measure admissible in the past
hypotheses.note: AdmissiblePastOn U nu: a measure on M carried by U, regular, finite, properties 3 and 4 with J^-_U, K^-_U for A subset of U. Proved: for nu a measure on the subspace U, AdmissiblePastOn U (map val nu) iff nu regular, finite, and properties 3/4 hold for nu on the val-preimages of J^-_U(q) minus J^-_U(p) and of J^-_U(A) minus K^-_U(A) (admissiblePastOn_map_subtype_iff, R1Space); every AdmissiblePastOn measure is such a push-forward (AdmissiblePastOn.exists_subtype). Not proved: that these traces are J^- and K^- of a causality on the type U (no restricted causality on a subtype exists in the library, kb/0001).

hypotheses.paper: (ii) q <= p implies K^-(q) subset K^-(p)
hypotheses.note: used for property 4 only; future form p <= q implies K^+(q) subset K^+(p), the time reversal

findings: ETT.tex:1094: 'strongly causal' is not used by the proof (l.1103-1139); hypothesis (i) already provides causally convex neighbourhoods. It can be dropped from the statement.
ETT.tex:1104: 'Since M is second countable' — only the Lindelöf property is used (a countable subcover of (U_p)).

ETT.tex:1106-1107: 'normalised so that mu_n(U_n)=1' is not always possible: a measure admissible in the past on U_n may be the zero measure (when U_n contains no pair p <_{U_n} q, property 3 is vacuous). Weights 2^{-n-1}/(1+mu_n(U_n)), or simply dropping zero terms, repair it.

ETT.tex:1110: 'Since each mu_n is a normalised regular Borel measure, mu is a regular Borel measure' is true but not immediate: outer regularity is not stable under the countable intersection of open sets the termwise argument would produce. It holds because the total mass is finite: inner regularity by closed sets passes to the sum (finite unions), and for a finite measure that gives outer regularity; this uses Hausdorff (R1). Proved as Causal.regular_sum.

ETT.tex:1111-1113: the existence of n_0, q' with p in U_{n_0}, p <_{U_{n_0}} q', q' <= q is correct: take the first link of the chain given by cor:causalement_connexe_minimal that leaves p (Causal.transGen_exists_first_ne).
Hypothesis (i) is necessary (admissiblePast_local_of_admissiblePast: U_p = M), so the proposition says that, under (ii), admissibility in the past is a local property for causally convex covers.
questions: (i) 'U_p carrying a measure admissible in the past' is read as a measure on the spacetime U_p (ex:open_subset), encoded as a measure on M carried by U_p. Proved: equivalent to a measure nu on the subspace U_p that is regular, finite, and satisfies properties 3 and 4 on the traces of J^-_{U_p}, K^-_{U_p} (admissiblePastOn_map_subtype_iff). That these traces are the J^-, K^- of the spacetime U_p rests on the library's convention of indexing by open sets (kb/0001); K^-_U agrees with the sequence definition inside U (mem_Kminus_singleton_iff_seq_mem). Confirm this is the intended meaning.
The future statement is read as the time reversal: (i) with measures admissible in the future, (ii) as 'for every p and every q >= p, K^+(q) subset K^+(p)'. Confirm.

kb_proposals: A measure on an open U seen as a spacetime is a Measure M with mu Uᶜ = 0 (Causal.Causality.AdmissiblePastOn); regular_map_subtype_val / exists_regular_subtype_of_compl_null transport regularity to and from the subtype (R1Space).

A countable sum of regular measures of finite total mass is regular: Causal.regular_sum (R1Space, BorelSpace); the route is InnerRegularWRT IsClosed IsOpen of the sum + InnerRegularWRT.weaklyRegular_of_finite (note the namespace).

Positive finite weights for a countable family of finite masses: ENNReal.exists_pos_tsum_mul_lt_of_countable, wrapped as Causal.exists_weights_tsum_lt; Measure.sum_apply_of_countable evaluates a countable sum on ANY set (property 4 is an outer-measure statement).
Second countability used for a countable subcover: ask LindelofSpace and use LindelofSpace.elim_nhds_subcover.
